entries.name: Dumbbell Flye
entries.reason: Source-bound flat draft: wide chest-plane shoulder arc, fixed15deg soft elbows and12.5/12 world arm lengths, two rigid neutral-grip dumbbells, head/back supported and quiet legs. Bench angle0deg and85deg opening are schematic draft choices, not universal ROM prescriptions. Independent technique/native runtime acceptance required.
entries.summary: Open through the shoulders with a fixed soft elbow bend, then hug the same arc closed.

frames.caption: Lie on a flat bench with feet on the floor; hold two bells over the chest with palms facing each other.
Open slowly in a wide shoulder arc; keep the same soft elbow bend.
Stop at a chest stretch you control, without dropping the shoulders deeper.
Keep the back and head supported and the elbow bend unchanged.
Hug the same arc closed over the chest; keep the bells apart.

entries.name: Flat Bench Cable Flyes
entries.reason: Source-bound draft, drawn from a 3D model turned 42 degrees so both low pulleys on either side of the centered flat bench, the wide open starting arc, the constant 156-degree elbow bend, and the cables lengthening as the hands sweep together above the chest all read clearly: starting wide with a soft elbow bend, sweeping the hands together above the chest, pausing at the top, and opening back out slowly.
entries.summary: Lying on a flat bench centered between two low pulleys with a D-handle in each hand and a soft, fixed bend in the elbows, begin with the arms wide, sweep the hands together in a wide arc above the chest, pause at the top, and open back out slowly.

frames.caption: Set a flat bench centered between two low pulleys, lie back holding a D-handle in each hand, and begin with the arms wide in a soft elbow bend.
Keeping the elbow angle constant, sweep the hands together in a wide arc above the chest.
Pause at the top with the hands together above the chest.
Open the arms back out slowly with a fixed bend in the elbows until you feel a stretch across the chest.
Control the stretch at the bottom with the arms wide before the next repetition.
